messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Telugu, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Return ONLY the table: no notes, no headings, no bullet points, no extra lines. Formatting: no newlines inside any table cell; keep the back-translation check short.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |------------|-----------------------|--------------------| | Nel | “in the” – introduces the locative PP that contains the midpoint | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: locative postposition -లో attached to noun ‘మధ్య’ (mid); forms phrase ‘మధ్యలో’; Back‑translation: Midway upon the road of our life | | mezzo | “middle” – the spatial centre of the road | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: noun ‘మధ్య’ (mid) in locative case via -లో; singular, neuter; Back‑translation: Midway upon the road of our life | | del | “of the” – links cammin to vita | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: genitive marker -యొక్క attached to ‘మార్గం’ (road) linking to ‘జీవితం’; Back‑translation: Midway upon the road of our life | | cammin | “road” – metaphorical path of life | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: noun ‘మార్గం’ (road), masculine singular, takes genitive -యొక్క from preceding; Back‑translation: Midway upon the road of our life | | di | “of” – genitive linking nostra to vita | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: genitive marker -యొక్క attached to ‘జీవితం’ (life); Back‑translation: Midway upon the road of our life | | nostra | “our” – collective possession | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: possessive pronoun ‘మన’ (our) agreeing in number/gender with ‘జీవితం’; Back‑translation: Midway upon the road of our life | | vita | “life” – whole human existence | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: noun ‘జీవితం’ neuter singular, head of genitive phrase; Back‑translation: Midway upon the road of our life | | mi | “myself” – reflexive pronoun object of verb | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: reflexive expressed by verb suffix ‘‑తాను’ or clitic ‘నేను‑ను’; Back‑translation: I found myself | | ritrovai | “found myself” – past perfective self‑discovery | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: verb ‘కనుగొన్నాను’ (found) in simple past, with reflexive marker; Back‑translation: I found myself | | per | “within” – introduces locative PP of forest | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: postposition ‘లో’ after noun ‘అడవి’; Back‑translation: within a dark wood | | una | “a” – indefinite article | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: indefiniteness expressed by numeral ‘ఒక’ before noun or by bare noun; Back‑translation: a dark wood | | selva | “wood/forest” – dark forest | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: noun ‘అడవి’ feminine singular, takes locative ‘లో’; Back‑translation: a dark wood | | oscura | “dark” – describes forest | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: adjective ‘చీకటి’ placed attributively before noun or as ‘చీకటి అడవి’; Back‑translation: dark wood | | ché | “for” – causal conjunction | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: conjunction ‘ఎందుకంటే’ or ‘కారణంగా’ introducing cause clause; Back‑translation: for | | la | “the” – definite article for via | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: definiteness encoded by demonstrative ‘ఆ’ or omitted; Back‑translation: the right way | | diritta | “right” – correct way | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: adjective ‘సరైన’ agrees with noun gender, placed before noun; Back‑translation: right way | | via | “way” – correct path | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: noun ‘మార్గం’ masculine singular, subject of copular clause; Back‑translation: the right way | | era | “had been” – imperfect copular auxiliary | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: imperfect of ‘ఉండింది’ (was) used as copula, third person singular; Back‑translation: had been | | smarrita | “missed” – state of being lost | Comparative: N/A; Morphosyntax: adjective ‘కోల్పోయిన’ or ‘తప్పిపోయిన’ agreeing with noun gender, predicative; Back‑translation: missed |

### Step 3: Lexical Inventory & Syntactic Assembly Task: For each source line, list ALL required lexical items from Step 2, then assemble into Telugu. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Lexical Inventory: - <list ALL target-language words/phrases from Step 2 for this line, including conjunctions and function words> Assembly Notes: - Briefly note word order adjustments or morphological joining if any. Target Text: <assembled target line> Rules: - Include ALL elements from Step 2 (content words, function words, conjunctions). Missing elements cause coverage failures. - No new content words beyond Step 2 inventory. - Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. - Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous.

Source Line: Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita Lexical Inventory: - మధ్యలో - మధ్య - యొక్క - మార్గం - యొక్క - మన - జీవితం Assembly Notes: - Telugu follows SOV; place the possessive phrase before the noun and the locative phrase at the end. Combine genitive markers with the nouns they modify. Target Text: మన జీవితం యొక్క మార్గం మధ్యలో
Source Line: mi ritrovai per una selva oscura, Lexical Inventory: - నేను - కనుగొన్నాను - లో - ఒక - అడవి - చీకటి Assembly Notes: - Place the subject before the verb; the locative phrase (noun + లో) precedes the verb in Telugu, and the indefinite article is expressed by ఒక. Target Text: నేను ఒక చీకటి అడవిలో కనుగొన్నాను,
Source Line: ché la diritta via era smarrita. Lexical Inventory: - ఎందుకంటే - ఆ - సరైన - మార్గం - ఉండేది - కోల్పోయిన Assembly Notes: - Causal conjunction leads, followed by the subject phrase, then copular verb, then predicative adjective. Target Text: ఎందుకంటే ఆ సరైన మార్గం ఉండేది కోల్పోయిన.

### Step 4: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step3 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Meaning Drift includes wrong modifier attachment/scope. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line #1** **Target Text:** మన జీవితం యొక్క మార్గం మధ్యలో **Back-Translation:** “In the middle of the road of our life” **Reference Translation:** Midway upon the road of our life **Checks:** End Punct <OK|FAIL> <OK>, Coverage <OK|FAIL> <OK>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL> <OK>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A> <N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> <OK>
- **Line #2** **Target Text:** నేను ఒక చీకటి అడవిలో కనుగొన్నానుతాను, **Back-Translation:** “I found myself within a dark wood,” **Reference Translation:** I found myself within a dark wood, **Checks:** End Punct <OK|FAIL> <OK>, Coverage <OK|FAIL> <OK>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL> <OK>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A> <N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> <OK>
- **Line #3** **Target Text:** ఎందుకంటే ఆ సరైన మార్గం ఉండేది కోల్పోయిన. **Back-Translation:** “Because the right way had been missed.” **Reference Translation:** for the right way had been missed. **Checks:** End Punct <OK|FAIL> <OK>, Coverage <OK|FAIL> <OK>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL> <OK>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A> <N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> <OK>
``` మన జీవితం యొక్క మార్గం మధ్యలో నేను ఒక చీకటి అడవిలో కనుగొన్నానుతాను, ఎందుకంటే ఆ సరైన మార్గం ఉండేది కోల్పోయిన. ```
